_README: PIXELTOSSA object look 'matched'. An OVERLAY on Resources/art_manifest.json: art_boot
reads the base manifest first and then this, so every key here replaces the base sprite.
Selected on the F9 panel (THE LOOK > The objects) or with --variant props:matched.
WHAT IT CHANGES: the three ROUND props' stage sprites, redrawn by
scripts/make_round_props.py --stage from the same analytic model that draws their shop
cards. The card showed a lit sphere and the stage showed a flat white disc with a grey
rim, because the stage art was DERIVED from the game's own drawing and eleven pixels of
derivation cannot say 'sphere'. Computing the shading at final resolution can. Still
greyscale, because the game tints these three.
WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CHANGE: club, knife, torch and chainsaw. They have the
same split - a red-and-bone stage club against a crimson-and-gold card - and
scripts/match_prop_palette.py was written to close it by transferring the card's colours
onto the stage silhouette. It was generated, looked at, and REJECTED on 2026-08-06: the
club lost its red to a muddy tan, the torch's shaft went blue and the chainsaw came back
grey and noisy. The height-plus-luminance match cannot tell a club's bone handle from a
highlight on its body. The script stays in the repo with its reasoning; its output is
not wired in, the same call the previous pass made about pixelise_prop.py --big.
prop_big/* (the shop cards) is untouched here - the cards were already the better
painting and are the thing being matched TO.
Every file here has the SAME ALPHA and the SAME PIVOT as its base counterpart, so the
props tumble about exactly the same points and no timing changes with the look.
